thread:
jules: Thinking about a less-invasive fail-mode: "partial admission" that is deadline-aware. Instead of flipping whole topology to microbatching, we decide per-request whether to join the continuous coalesce or take a tiny dedicated window based on deadline slack.

neha: Interesting. So admit() needs to know soft_deadline and maybe an estimate of remaining tokens?

jules: Yup. admit(req) -> {route: COALESCE|TINY_WINDOW|IMMEDIATE, reason}. COALESCE tries to batch as usual. TINY_WINDOW prefers 1-4 request windows. IMMEDIATE bypasses batching entirely for latency-critical tiny calls.

pavan: How do we compute deadline slack cheaply? We can use client_provided deadline_ms OR infer from token_count_estimate + configured per-token ms. Keep it simple initially.

zack: We must avoid adding per-request heavy calc. Suggest admit(req, hints={deadline_ms, estimated_tokens}) where hints is optional. Runtime uses hints when present, otherwise fallback to size-based heuristics.

neha: Operator control: allow per-tenant min_mode and max_mode overrides (e.g., tenant A always COALESCE, tenant B can be demoted). Also a cluster-level circuit-breaker if p95 overall > SLO.

jules: One tricky bit: coalescer fairness. If many requests choose TINY_WINDOW, we fragment batch efficiency. We should cap percent of TINY_WINDOW slots per epoch to preserve throughput. Eg tiny_window_budget_per_epoch = 0.15 of total slots.

pavan: Nice. Implementation idea: admission returns route plus a budget_token if routing to TINY_WINDOW. The coalescer enforces budget consumption with atomic counters per-epoch. If budget exhausted, route falls back to COALESCE or IMMEDIATE depending on slack.

zack: Hysteresis: allow a tenant to get consecutive tiny windows up to N times before forcing a backoff. Prevents gaming.

neha: Observability: events must record why a request was diverted: reason codes like DEADLINE_SLACK_LOW, KV_MISS_HEAVY, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Metrics: batch.efficiency, tiny_window.usage, tiny_window.denied.

jules: Security/private deploys: all heuristics run locally; no telemetry exported unless customer enables. Config flags: --enable-partial-admit, --tiny-budget=0.1.

pavan: Corner case: multi-turn streaming. Admission decision must be sticky for streaming session; if demoted mid-stream you may lose cache affinity. So sticky decisions keyed by session_id with short TTL.

zack: Also add a fallback transition: if cluster-level KV miss spike detected, shrink tiny_window_budget to 0.02 to force more aggressive coalescing and protect throughput. That's the opposite of earlier strategies but may reduce wasted compute.

neha: Test plan: sim harness with a mix of tiny latency-critical calls and large long-gen calls; measure p99 and tokens/sec with different budgets. Expectation: p99 of latency-critical calls <= target while throughput loss < 10% at default budget.

jules: Small config sketch:```
partial_admit.enabled = true
partial_admit.tiny_budget = 0.15
partial_admit.min_tiny_window_tokens = 1
partial_admit.max_consecutive_tiny = 3
partial_admit.cluster_kv_spike_shrink = 0.02
```

pavan: Backwards compatible: admit signature optional hints. We'll ship behind feature flag.

zack: I'll prototype the budget token counter in the coalescer and expose metrics.

neha: I'll add Console annotations for diverted requests and per-tenant budgets. Also add an operator API `rdbctl batcher budget set <tenant|cluster> <fraction>` for incident control.

deploy-bot: deploybot: canary rollout queued: batcher-partial-admit-v0.1 -> canary. Logs -> /observability/partial_admit.

jules: Thanks, team. If canary looks good we can tune defaults and wire Optimize to recommend budgets based on workload shape. :rocket:
